description:
(1) Demolition of existing rear conservatory and
construction of a single storey rear extension. (2) Construction of a first
floor side/ rear extension. (3) Alterations to fenestration to include
alteration to the opening of existing first floor front window to facilitate
the installation of a window. (4) Alteration to existing garage door opening at
principle elevation to facilitate the installation of a window or door and
alterations to the rear door opening to facilitate the installation of a
window.
decision_conditions: The application as submitted comprises of inconsistent plans relating to (i) The proposed ground floor plan closest to the boundary with No. 63 illustrates 2No. windows and the existing door being retained at the side elevation. However, the proposed side elevation has been illustrated with windows only and fails to reference the existing door (the existing kitchen has not been included on the the proposed side elevation and therefore the overall depth is also incorrect) (ii) The proposed front elevation (drawing No. AA-65-Whipps-01P) has been illustrated with the garage door replaced with a window. However, the proposed front elevation (drawing No. AA-65-whipps-03P) including the neighbouring dwellings has been illustrated with a door. As such it is not possible to establish that the development complies with Policy 53 of the Waltham Forest Local Plan Pt 1 (2024).

Notwithstanding the first point of refusal, the proposed extension(s) would be of a poor appearance and design when viewed in relation with the proposed works at first floor level the combined relationship is considered lamentable. These incongruous extensions when grouped together obliterate key characteristics of the host dwelling appearing as excessively large and bulky additions and would not appear subservient to the host building. The proposal is therefore considered contrary to Policy 53 of the Waltham Forest Local Plan Pt 1 (2024).

In the absence of a Tree Survey (in line with British Standard 5837:2012 Trees in Relation to Design, Demolition and Construction) and an Arboricultural Method Statement, to identify the impact of the development on the existing trees on site and any other trees located within the vicinity of the development site, along with the required protection and mitigation measures, a full assessment of the acceptability of the development and assurance of the protection of local biodiversity cannot be carried out, and therefore it cannot be confirmed that the development would be in compliance with ﻿Policy 80 of the Waltham Forest Local Plan Pt 1 (2024).
site_name: 65 Whipps Cross Road, Leytonstone, London, E11 1NJ
